should_fix.issue: Key takeaways barely name the traditions; the box most scanners read says 'a sequence of family customs'. Brief requires exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways. r2 lines: "- A traditional Macedonian wedding is a sequence of family customs that can begin months before the church service and end with the oro on the dance floor." and "- Customs vary by village, region and family, and Macedonian-Australian families often adapt them, so ask your own family which ones matter to them."
should_fix.fix: Keep exactly 4 bullets, one sentence each. Replace bullet 1 with: "- A traditional Macedonian wedding often runs from the formal asking and the engagement through the gifts, the wedding flag and the bread, collecting the bride and the Orthodox crowning, to the welcome at the groom's home and the oro." Keep bullet 2 (kum and kuma) as is. Replace bullet 3 with: "- Customs vary by village, region and family, and in the mountain village of Galičnik one selected couple is still married each year in the traditional regional style at the Galičnik Wedding Festival." Keep bullet 4 (registry office and Embassy Belgrade) unchanged as the legal and travel takeaway. All wording from sourced body lines (intro running order, fact_01, fact_03); no new facts. Ranked should_fix despite one flag because it carries a brief must_include for the secondary persona.

should_fix.issue: Older and less mobile guests at a mountain or village wedding: no prompt on access. r2 line: "For a mountain or village wedding, season matters. Smartraveller notes bush and forest fires from June to September, and very low temperatures, snow and ice from October to March. <!-- fact_103 --> The emergency number is 112. <!-- fact_110 -->"
should_fix.fix: Add one sentence after this paragraph, phrased only as questions to ask: "If older or less mobile guests are coming, ask the venue or your planner about the altitude, any steps or steep paths between the church and the reception, how guests will be transferred, and check their travel insurance covers them." No claims about any venue's access, distances or terrain.

should_fix.issue: 'Wikipedia's account' reads as low-authority and makes the brand sound unsure of its subject. r2 line: "Wikipedia's account describes it as symbolising the farewell of villagers leaving home to work abroad. <!-- fact_06 -->"
should_fix.fix: Change to: "One published account describes it as symbolising the farewell of villagers leaving home to work abroad. <!-- fact_06 -->" Keep the attribution hedge and the fact marker; do not state the meaning as fact.

consider.issue: The Galičnik 'one couple' fact is the best 'did not know' payoff but sits mid-section after timing details. r2 line: "One couple is married each year. Accounts differ on who can enter, so treat any eligibility rule you read as unconfirmed. <!-- fact_03 --> <!-- fact_07 --> Either way, it is a cultural event to watch, not a venue a visiting couple can book."
consider.fix: Move "One couple is married each year." (with fact_03) to directly after "For a sense of how one region keeps its customs alive, look to Galičnik." Keep the eligibility hedge and the 'not a venue' line where they are. The takeaway above also surfaces it early; do not add it to the intro as well unless it reads naturally.

consider.issue: Repeated 'often told' plus 'ask your family' closers feel like hedging stacked on hedging. r2 line: "The meanings attached to that moment are often told rather than recorded, and they differ by family, so ask whoever is baking what it means to them."
consider.fix: Do not add meanings and do not remove 'often told' labels (sourcing rule). Only trim the duplicate 'ask your family' tail where a section already says customs vary, e.g. end this line at "...often told rather than recorded, and they differ by family." Light touch, at most two such trims across the piece.
